messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a spike in fncall validation rejects this morning after the explainability tag landed in the model adapter. Rejects map to strict schema failures, not runtime errors.
maya: Can you paste an example of the rejected payload?
alex: sure — minimal reproduce: 
```json
{
  \"tool\": \"search\",\n  \"result\": { \"items\": [] },\n  \"explainability\": { \"method\": \"shap\", \"weights\": null }
}
```
validator complains because weights: null vs weights: number[] in the schema. We added explainability as required in the onboarding PR (my bad).
drew: oof. Is this hitting production users or just internal canary?
alex: production traffic. Volume is small but noisy — 0.7% of fncall responses in EU region for the morning window. Quota/route isn't affected but console is showing a jump in reject alerts.
sasha: The UX is bad: console alerts a full-on error and oncall gets paged via the rule we set for schema spikes. We need a less noisy signal for explainability mismatches.
khanh: Two angles: 1) make explainability.weights nullable in schema (fast), or 2) switch validator to a soft-validate mode for that field and surface a warning in telemetry/console (safer). Thoughts?
evan: prefer 2 for correctness. Some models will legitimately return null when they can't compute explanations; we shouldn't silently accept broken arrays. Soft-validate + metric tag would let us monitor.
maya: Agree with soft-validate. We should also add an explicit telemetry tag on the request/response so routing/consume teams can filter. Something like `fncall.explainability.status = (ok|null|malformed)`.
alex: implementation note: validator currently returns 400-like structured reject and increments schema_rejects metric with route label. We can add a new metric `fncall.explainability_status` and set: ok, null, malformed. Then console can show a per-route chart.
sasha: And temporarily mute the pager rule for the schema spike alarm if the spike is mostly explainability.malformed. Ops-bot can create a suppression window.
ops-bot: deploy suppression created: rule schema-spike-eu muted for 2 hours by sasha (reason: explainability soft rollout).
drew: For rollout UX: we should add a Console banner on affected routes that says "Explainability field is in soft-validate; some responses may be missing weights." Link to docs and a toggle to re-enable strict validation per-route.
khanh: We also need to think about quotas: some downstream tooling bills on token counts of explainability arrays. If weights are null we should avoid counting those tokens in billing heuristics. That likely needs a billing PR.
evan: I'll prototype the validator flag: soft_validate_fields: ["explainability.weights"] and emit tags. If we expose that as a canary config key we can flip per-route without a full deploy.
maya: Nice — add a sampling rate for telemetry (e.g., sample 1% of malformed payloads) so we can get exemplars without too much PII.
alex: Action items: 1) evan add soft-validate toggle + telemetry tags (ETA today), 2) sasha create pager suppression + console banner copy (done for suppression), 3) khanh open billing ticket for token counting change, 4) maya add sampling config and docs snippet. I'll roll back the schema PR to make explainability optional if we still see production rejects after soft rollout.
sasha: Sounds good. Can we also add a short-lived dashboard: per-route explainability_status and example payloads (redacted)? That will help Product see impact.
evan: will push a canary config and post canary link here when ready.
ops-bot: canary deploy started by evan -> canary-id ctry-430123. Logs: https://internal.ci/canary/ctry-430123
alex: thanks. keep updates small — we'll watch metrics for the next 2 hours and reconvene if reject rate > 1.5%.
